title: Recover delegation findings from severity-count summaries
outcome: Delegated reviewers can emit a contradictory packet whose Summary says 'Found one High-severity fail-open condition' while Findings says None. Parser v4 only recognizes finding nouns such as issue/bug/risk, so it trusts the empty section and the parent fan-in loses an actionable finding. Add structural detection for found/identified/detected + positive count + severity, preserve resolved/clean negations, bump the parser version so retained completed children are reparsed, and add an exact regression test for the observed Codex wording.
acceptance: The observed 'Found one High-severity fail-open condition' packet recovers its actionable preamble finding; clean/resolved summaries remain empty; retained terminal records with a recorded result are not reparsed after parser changes, reviewer terminal truth comes only from validated submission envelopes, and the prose parser serves ordinary explorer/worker children.

Summary diagnostics classify sentences with qualifying attached severities using the documented closed POSITIVE/CLEAN/UNRESOLVED contract. Non-clean sentences report the highest qualifying severity regardless of order; whole-sentence clean/resolved templates produce no contradiction diagnostic; unmatched mentions, including ambiguous negation, remain visible as diagnostics without inventing structured findings. Explicit structured findings and AsBefore preamble recovery are unchanged.
